clue.text: Side effects of accident abroad

parts.note: a fall is an accident, a tumble
out and abroad both mean away from home

explanation.surface: Someone abroad suffers the aftermath of an accident.
explanation.definitionFit: Fallout is the unwelcome consequences that follow an event, its side effects.

clue.text: Announcement concerning catering at football ground?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a flourish of trumpets heralding someone
second meaning, split in two: the food sold to supporters is their fare

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags a whimsical reading: food for the fans at a match would be fan fare.
explanation.definitionFit: A fanfare is a short burst of trumpets announcing an arrival, so a showy announcement.

clue.text: Medication presents zero alternative before cuts ordered

indicators.note: before means coming first, so this piece leads
the alternative form of the word is taken here as its other direction, giving its letters back to front

parts.note: nil is zero

indicators.note: ordered means arranged, so the letters of cuts are put in a new order

parts.note: anagram fodder, taken as written

explanation.surface: A doctor offers a choice: take this medicine or face surgical cuts.
explanation.walkthrough: The setter probably meant a rearrangement of NIL; reversing it gives the same LIN. 'ordered' turns CUTS into CTUS.
explanation.definitionFit: Linctus is a syrupy cough medicine, a kind of medication.

clue.text: Scoundrel has no right, the beast

indicators.note: having none of something means it is removed from the word

parts.note: a rotter is a scoundrel
R is the abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: A scoundrel with no sense of right is called a beast.
explanation.walkthrough: Rotter is old-fashioned British slang for a scoundrel.
explanation.definitionFit: The otter is a river mammal, so it is an example of a beast or animal.

clue.text: Performer's bound to make an impact?

definitions.text: Performer's bound to make an impact?

parts.words: Performer's bound to make an impact?
parts.note: surface reading: this entertainer is sure to impress; setter's reading: a performer whose every bound and step strikes the floor, making noise

explanation.walkthrough: 'Bound' looks like 'certain' and 'impact' like 'impression'; read literally, it is a leap that strikes the floor, as metal-soled shoes do.
explanation.definitionFit: This dancer wears shoes with metal plates and makes rhythms by striking the floor with them.

clue.text: Behaves in a masterly way

parts.note: surface reading: acts with skill and command; setter's reading: acts as a schoolmaster does in the classroom

explanation.walkthrough: Masterly suggests virtuoso skill, but a master is also a schoolteacher, and what a schoolmaster does is instruct a class.
explanation.definitionFit: Instructing pupils is the work of a schoolmaster, so to act like one is to instruct.

clue.text: Saying thanks at outset shows good judgement

indicators.note: at outset says this piece is moved to stand at the very start

parts.note: ta is British informal for thank you
to state something is to say it

explanation.surface: Saying thank you right at the start shows good judgement.
explanation.walkthrough: Take TA out of STATE to leave STE, then put TA at the outset. Ta is a casual British thank-you.
explanation.definitionFit: Taste is discernment in matters of style and quality, a sense of good judgement.

clue.text: Scrapped a prohibition order against two men

parts.note: taken as written
a ban is an order prohibiting something
Don and Ed are two men's names

explanation.surface: A prohibition order against two men was scrapped.
explanation.definitionFit: Something abandoned has been given up and discarded, so scrapped.

clue.text: Arrogance shown by hospital director

parts.note: H is the abbreviation for hospital, as on road signs
an auteur is a film director with a distinctive personal style

explanation.surface: A hospital director shows arrogance.
explanation.definitionFit: Hauteur is haughtiness, a proud and superior manner.

clue.text: Believe it's stupid to accept law being overturned

indicators.note: accepting something means taking it in, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: slow means dim-witted

indicators.note: overturned means turned upside down, so in a down entry the word reads back up

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone believes it is foolish to accept a law being overturned.
explanation.definitionFit: To swallow a story is to accept it as true without question, to believe it.

clue.text: Constant refusal for directions to summit

parts.note: a refusal is a no
N and S, north and south, are compass directions
the summit is the top

explanation.surface: A climber is repeatedly refused directions to a mountain summit.
explanation.definitionFit: Something nonstop continues without a break, so it is constant.

clue.text: Stir up salt with a cooking utensil

indicators.note: stirring mixes contents around, so the letters that follow are jumbled

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A recipe instruction: stir the salt in with a utensil.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stir up' looks like one phrasal verb, but only 'Stir' signals the mix; 'up' is part of the letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A spatula is a flat-bladed kitchen tool used for spreading and turning food.

clue.text: Every other officer in near chaos at the end

indicators.note: one thing sitting in another means it is placed inside it

parts.note: taken as written
Lt is the abbreviation for lieutenant, an officer

indicators.note: chaos is disorder, so the word beside it is thrown into a jumbled order

parts.note: the letters of near, rearranged

indicators.note: the end of a word is its final letter, the only one kept

parts.note: the final letter of the

explanation.surface: An officer finds things nearly chaotic by the end.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Near chaos' reads as 'almost chaos', but 'near' is the word to be jumbled, with the officer slipped inside it. Lt is the standard abbreviation for lieutenant.
explanation.definitionFit: Alternate as an adjective means every second one, as in alternate days.

clue.text: To live with daughter is fine

parts.note: D is the standard abbreviation for daughter
fine and well both describe good health

explanation.surface: Living with one's daughter is a perfectly fine arrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: To dwell somewhere is to reside or make a home there.

clue.text: Stand adopted by artist

parts.note: surface reading: a position or stance an artist takes up; setter's reading: a physical frame a painter uses to hold the canvas

explanation.walkthrough: 'Stand adopted' sounds like an opinion or principle an artist holds; read literally it is the wooden support a painter works at.
explanation.definitionFit: An easel is the upright frame that holds a painter's canvas while they work.

clue.text: Look up name on sign for bookkeeper

indicators.note: on here means placed next to, so these pieces follow the other

parts.note: Libra is a sign of the zodiac

indicators.note: in a down entry, going up means the word reads from bottom to top

parts.note: an air is a look or appearance
N is the abbreviation for name

explanation.surface: Looking up a name on a sign to find the bookkeeper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bookkeeper' wants to be an accountant; it is the person who keeps a library's books.
explanation.definitionFit: A librarian is in charge of a library, literally a keeper of books.

clue.text: Flighty lot get taxi home with team

parts.note: a cab is a taxi
someone at home is in
a crew is a team

explanation.surface: A flighty group takes a taxi home together with their team.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flighty' suggests fickle people, but here it means those who work on flights.
explanation.definitionFit: The staff who look after passengers on aeroplane flights are a group of people working aloft.

clue.text: Partner strangely fiery in relationship

indicators.note: in means placed within, so the rearranged letters go inside the word for relationship

parts.note: a bond is a close relationship

indicators.note: strangely signals that the letters of fiery appear in an odd order

parts.note: anagram fodder, taken as written

explanation.surface: A partner behaves oddly passionately within a relationship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'strangely' turns FIERY into YFRIE, which goes between BO and ND.
explanation.definitionFit: A boyfriend is a male romantic partner.

clue.text: File by, slip inside for some fruit

parts.note: a rasp is a coarse file

indicators.note: something inside goes within the other word, splitting it

parts.note: taken as written
to slip is to make a mistake, to err

explanation.surface: Instructions to file something, with a slip tucked inside, while fruit picking.
explanation.definitionFit: A raspberry is a soft red berry, so it names one kind of fruit.

clue.text: Know being sincere is to the point

parts.note: real feelings are sincere ones
taken as written
E, east, is a compass point

explanation.surface: Knowing that being sincere is to the point.
explanation.definitionFit: To realise something is to become aware of it, to understand or know it.

clue.text: He's out to score

parts.note: surface reading: someone intent on getting what they want; setter's reading: a worker on a walkout is out, and a football forward's job is to score goals

explanation.walkthrough: Two readings meet: a worker out on a walkout, and the forward in football whose role is scoring goals.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a worker who has walked out in protest and a football forward who tries for goals.

clue.text: Dominate mixed ward at formal opening

indicators.note: mixed means jumbled together, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: the letters of ward, rearranged

indicators.note: the opening of a word is its first letter, the only one kept

parts.note: the first letter of formal

explanation.surface: Someone takes charge of a mixed hospital ward at its formal opening.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mixed ward' reads as a hospital ward for both sexes; 'mixed' is really the signal to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: To dwarf something is to tower over it, making it look small, so to dominate it.

clue.text: Put out at Mavis reverting to type

indicators.note: put out means disturbed, so these letters are disturbed into a new order

explanation.surface: Mavis is upset and goes back to her old ways.
explanation.walkthrough: AT stays as written; MAVIS rearranged gives AVISM.
explanation.definitionFit: Atavism is the return of ancestral traits, a throwback to an earlier form.

clue.text: Having nothing to do as I arranged the flower

parts.note: being free means having no commitments

indicators.note: arranged means set out in order, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: anagram fodder, taken as written
anagram fodder, taken as written

explanation.surface: With time on my hands, I did the flower arranging.
explanation.walkthrough: 'arranged' looks like flower arranging, but it rearranges AS and I into SIA.
explanation.definitionFit: A freesia is a fragrant African plant grown for its bright blooms.

clue.text: First organised rota for one giving blood

parts.note: A is the first letter of the alphabet

indicators.note: something organised is put into a new order, so the word is rearranged

parts.note: the letters of rota, rearranged

explanation.surface: The first thing organised is a rota for blood donors.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One giving blood' sounds like a donor, but it is the great artery that supplies blood from the heart to the body.
explanation.definitionFit: The aorta is the main artery carrying blood out of the heart to the rest of the body.

clue.text: Graduate carried out the defence

parts.note: BA, Bachelor of Arts, is a graduate

indicators.note: out means wrong or disordered, so the letters of carried are rearranged

parts.note: anagram fodder, taken as written

explanation.surface: A graduate executed the defence strategy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'carried out' looks like a phrase meaning executed, but 'out' is the anagram signal on CARRIED.
explanation.definitionFit: A barricade is a makeshift barrier set up as a defensive obstruction.

clue.text: Go back in vehicle — not the genuine article

indicators.note: something in a vehicle sits inside it, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: a bus is a vehicle

indicators.note: going back means travelling the other way, so the word reads backwards

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Returning in a vehicle that turns out to be a fake.
explanation.definitionFit: Something bogus is a sham or counterfeit, so it is not real.

clue.text: Perfect one to do business with

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
to deal with someone is to do business with them

explanation.surface: The perfect person to do business with.
explanation.definitionFit: Ideal as an adjective means flawless, exactly as good as could be wished.

clue.text: Timeless sound gives one idea

indicators.note: read as time-less, it says the sound is without time, so that letter goes

parts.note: a tinkling is a light ringing sound
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: A sound without a sense of time gives someone an idea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Timeless' looks like one adjective; split it as 'time' plus 'less', and the T comes off the front of the sound.
explanation.definitionFit: An inkling is a slight hint or vague notion, a faint idea of something.

clue.text: Pupils hide behind them

parts.note: surface reading: schoolchildren take cover behind something; setter's reading: the dark centres of the eyes, covered when the eyes close

explanation.walkthrough: Pupils suggests schoolchildren ducking behind desks; the pupils are really parts of the eye, hidden behind the folds of skin that close over it.
explanation.definitionFit: The folds of skin that close over the eyeball cover the pupil when someone blinks or sleeps.

clue.text: German chap takes hour off — and son gets chores!

indicators.note: takes ... off means removes, so the item named is dropped from the word before

parts.note: Herr is the German for Mr, a German man's title
H is the abbreviation for hour
taken as written
S is the abbreviation for son

explanation.surface: A German father takes an hour off work, and his son is left with the housework.
explanation.definitionFit: Errands are short trips to do jobs such as shopping, everyday tasks or chores.

clue.text: Cover reflected novel predicament

indicators.note: a reflection in a mirror shows things the wrong way round

parts.note: a lid is a cover
Emma is the Jane Austen novel

explanation.surface: A book's cover mirrors the dilemma at the heart of the novel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Novel' looks like an adjective meaning new, but it stands for a particular novel, Austen's Emma.
explanation.definitionFit: A dilemma is a difficult situation needing a choice between bad options, a predicament.
